topic: Understanding Discrete Convolutions: From Filters to Features
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Engineering students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Sliding Window Concept (0:45)
lecture_lines: Data is organized in a grid.
We scan with a small window.
The window looks at local neighborhoods.
animations: 1. Display 1D array on screen with color #FFFFFF.
2. Slide a small window across the array.
3. Highlight elements within the window in #FF4500.
4. Move window element by element, updating the highlight.
5. Fade out window, keep final array state.

sections.title: Defining Discrete Convolution (1:15)
lecture_lines: We flip, slide, multiply, and sum.
The kernel slides over the input.
Each overlap creates one output value.
This forms a new feature map.
animations: 1. Define formula (f * g)[n] = Σ f[k]g[n-k]. Display in #00FFFF.
2. Show function f and kernel g as arrays.
3. Flip kernel g horizontally, show in #FFFF00.
4. Slide kernel g over f, calculate sum-product.

sections.title: The 'Effect' of the Kernel (1:30)
animations: 1. Show a blurry image, display 'Input' in #FFFFFF.
2. Apply a sharpening kernel, show in #FF00FF.
3. Display the resulting sharp image, label 'Output' in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Image Processing & AI (1:00)
animations: 1. Show a convolutional neural network layer diagram.

sections.title: Conclusion & Summary (0:30)
lecture_lines: It maps inputs to useful features.
animations: 2. Fade in 'Convolution is a sliding process' in #00FF00.
